text.title: AI Pre-Screen Bias Guardrails — Worked Examples
text.summary: One complete guardrail spec for an LLM-graded backend take-home, with a note on every value a reader might question, and one spec for the same pipeline as it was first built that breaks seven subject rules and what the validator and the legal reviewer say about it.

section.title: Scenario
section.p: An engineering team uses an LLM to grade backend take-homes before the hiring manager reads them. Candidates apply from New York, California and Germany. Legal asked for a written guardrail before any candidate is scored. The team runs steps 1-9 of `content/04-procedure.xml` and files the spec below.

example.title: Complete spec, no stage on hold
example.note: `redaction.stripped_attributes` lists all ten classes even though take-homes rarely carry a photo: the schema requires the full set because the redaction function is shared with the CV pre-screen, and the class that is "never there" is the one that leaks.

`calibration.threshold` 0.65 was recorded before the run and `result` 0.71 came after; the spec carries both so a reviewer can see the threshold was not chosen to fit the number (fm-calibration-on-synthetic-cvs is about provenance, r-calibration-sample-before-go-live is about order).
Two anchors per criterion would not validate: `anchors` requires low, mid and high, because a rubric with only the endpoints lets the model invent the middle of the scale per candidate.

`adverse_impact.per_stage` has two stages: the system filters at "forwarded to hiring manager" and again influences "advanced to onsite" through its score, so both are monitored. `min_ratio` 0.87 on the second stage is above 0.8, so `on_hold` is false.

`legal.applicable_law` is nyc-ll-144 because one jurisdiction is New York; the notice lead is exactly the 10 business days the DCWP rules require and the bias audit date is inside the preceding year of `first_score_at`.
`pinned_tuple.rubric_version` and `redaction_version` equal the versions in their own sections; the tuple is what step 8 compares against the last calibration run.

section.title: Bad example: the same pipeline as first built

example.title: Seven subject rules broken
example.note: What the validator prints: `redaction.stripped_attributes: 3 items is under minItems 10` and `unit_tested: False is not the required const True` (r-protected-attributes-stripped-before-model); `rubric.written_before_first_score: False` and three anchors under minLength 10 (r-rubric-versioned-before-first-score); `proxy_review.proxy_terms_found: 2 items is over maxItems 0` (r-no-proxy-criteria-in-prompt); `calibration.sample_source: 'synthetic-cvs' is not the required const 'real-applicant-pool'`, `human_reviewers: 1 is below minimum 2`, `threshold_set_before_run: False` (r-calibration-sample-before-go-live); `adverse_impact.per_stage[0].on_hold: False is not the required const True` because min_ratio 0.67 is under 0.8 (r-adverse-impact-monitored-per-stage); `human_of_record.auto_reject_filter_present: True`, `decision_carries_role_handle: False`, `reviewer_inputs: 1 items is under minItems 2` (r-human-of-record-decides); `legal: missing required field: notice_text_url`, `missing required field: bias_audit`, `notice_lead_business_days: 3 is below minimum 10` (r-candidate-notice-and-bias-audit); `audit_log.fields: 2 items is under minItems 7`, `retention_months: 3 is below minimum 12`, `queryable_per_candidate: False` (r-per-candidate-audit-log-retained); `pinned_tuple.model_id: 'gpt-4o-latest' matches the forbidden not schema`.

What the legal reviewer sees beyond the validator: a kappa of 0.92 on synthetic CVs next to a real-pool selection ratio of 0.67 is the signature of fm-calibration-on-synthetic-cvs — the system agrees with itself and disagrees with the applicant pool. With an auto-reject filter in place, every candidate rejected since first_score_at needs a backfilled human decision and, in New York, a notice. The spec goes back to step 1.

list.item: Order is the control: redaction before scoring, rubric before the first score, threshold before the calibration number. The spec records dates so the order is checkable.
The four-fifths hold is a schema consequence: a stage ratio under 0.8 forces on_hold true, so the table cannot be attached without the hold being visible.
The pinned tuple is what turns "we upgraded the model for cost" into a calibration re-run instead of a silent change.
